Lina: Heads-up: nightly DAST flagged a reflected XSS on /upload in the staging pipeline. SAST shows no issues.
Lina: Scanner logs show it couldn't fetch the hashed artifact: `KMS AccessDenied for decrypt key=alias/ci-artifact-key principal=arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/scan-runner`
Tom: That usually means the scanner ran against an HTML error page instead of the real bundle -> false positive.
Diego: Agree. We should avoid editing the key policy. Two safe options: create a short-lived KMS grant for the scanner or switch the scanner to use a presigned S3 URL for the artifact.
Anya: Compliance wants full auditability. If we use grants, will CloudTrail capture Decrypt events tied to the scanner role?
Tom: Yes. CloudTrail logs KMS:Decrypt and Unwrap events. When using a grant, the Decrypt shows up with the grantee principal. Example log: `EventName=Decrypt userIdentity=scan-runner keyId=alias/ci-artifact-key`
Lina: Any RBAC changes needed? The scanner runs under scan-service-role attached to ephemeral runners.
Diego: No long-lived key-policy changes. CreateGrant is preferred for ephemeral access. Key policy stays untouched.
Anya: If we go grants, can we restrict by VPC endpoint or a request tag? We want to ensure only CI jobs can use it.
Tom: Yes, grants can include conditions. Example condition: `StringEquals: { \"aws:SourceVpce\": \"vpce-0a1b2c\" }` or `StringEquals: { \"aws:RequestTag/scan_job\": \"nightly\" }`. That plus retiring the grant after the job is good.
Lina: Who can retire grants? We need automation to avoid orphaned grants.
Diego: The actor that created the grant gets the grantId and can call RetireGrant. We'll add a post-job cleanup step in the CI job that calls `kms.retire_grant`. Alternatively a small Lambda on job-complete event can retire it.
Anya: Can we prove retirement to auditors? What logs show retirement?
Tom: RetireGrant is a KMS management API; CloudTrail records it as `RetireGrant` with the caller identity and grantId. Keep the grantId in the CI job artifacts for evidence.
security-bot: Note: staging-dast-2026-03-20-22 started at 2026-03-20T22:00:00Z and errored at 2026-03-20T22:05:14Z.
Lina: For quick unblock, can someone create a grant, run the scanner, and retire it? I'd prefer to avoid changing artifact flow in the middle of release.
Diego: I can create the grant and retire it. Will post grantId and CloudTrail sample.
ci-bot: Rerun triggered: staging-dast-2026-03-20-22 (rerun by Diego)
Diego: Grant created: `grantId=gr-0a1b2c3d4e5f` (created 2026-03-20T22:10:02Z).
Diego: Scanner run complete; no XSS findings. Retiring grant now.
Diego: Grant retired: `retireGrantId=gr-0a1b2c3d4e5f` (retired 2026-03-20T22:12:40Z). CloudTrail snippet: `2026-03-20T22:11:15Z CloudTrail Event: Decrypt principal=arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/scan-runner keyId=alias/ci-artifact-key requestId=req-456`
Lina: Verified. Findings are gone. Thanks Diego.
Anya: Follow-up action: migrate DAST to presigned S3 URLs in the next sprint to remove KMS dependency. Also update the Secure SDLC checklist to state: \"Scanners must not require CMK decrypt unless approved for short-lived grants and audited.\"
Tom: I'll draft the ephemeral-grant runbook: create-grant -> run-scan -> retire-grant -> collect CloudTrail evidence -> store grantId in job artifacts.
sre-oncall: I'll add an alert rule to watch for unusual Decrypt volumes from the scan-runner principal during rollout windows. Threshold: >5 Decrypts/min from unexpected source.
Lina: Also we should add a note for reviewers: if SAST is clean and DAST fails on a static asset, flag for artifact access failure before triaging as vuln. saves time.
Diego: Filed ticket: INFRA-1248 to implement presigned artifact flow and INFRA-1249 to add retire-grant automation. Linking from this thread.
Lina: Closing this thread. Will attach the CI logs and CloudTrail snippet to the ticket. :white_check_mark:
